_note: Aditya Birla Capital, lender model on the STANDALONE accounts (screener.json basis = standalone): since the merger of Aditya Birla Finance (effective 1-Apr-2025, appointed date 1-Apr-2024; FY24 restated) ABCL itself is the NBFC, and it carries its subsidiaries and associates at cost (₹8,991 cr at Mar-26) and receives the AMC's dividend. The consolidated accounts mix ~₹29,000 cr of life-insurance premium and claims with lending income, which the lender engine cannot represent, so the housing-finance company, the insurers, the AMC and the rest are valued outside the engine in a sum of the parts (sotp block below; built in tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.ctx.js). Consolidated EPS (the street's basis) is rebuilt in the ctx file as model PAT − AMC dividend + share of each subsidiary's profit. AUM = NBFC lending AUM.

history._why: aum = NBFC AUM at March (Q4FY25 and Q4FY26 presentations; FY24 from the Q4FY24 presentation). provisions = impairment on financial instruments in the standalone P&L (Annual Report FY26 for FY25-26; FY25 annual report's restated FY24). feeIncome = Screener standalone revenue less the annual report's interest income: dividends (AMC ₹311 cr in FY26), fees and commission (incl. insurance distribution), fair-value gains, assignment gains and, in FY24-25, the gains on selling AMC shares (₹636 cr and ₹283 cr). Screener revenue is ₹15-40 cr above the annual report in FY24-25 (it adds part of other income).

src.aum: Q4FY26 presentation p19 (4-May-2026); Q4FY25 p24; Q4FY24 p21
src.provisions/fees: Annual Report FY26 standalone P&L (note 27-35); Annual Report FY25 (FY24 restated)

base._why: 2,61,96,06,094 shares at 31-Mar-2026 (Annual Report FY26, directors' report and note on share capital).

_aumGrowthWhy: NBFC AUM grew 27% in FY26 and 28% YoY in Q1FY27 (5% QoQ) with disbursements +34%. Management has funded three years of NBFC growth with the June raise (87.5% of ₹4,000 cr) and starts gold loans in Q2FY27 (200-300 branches in FY27). We assume 25% / 23% / 21%: a little below the current pace because the book is now ₹1.67 lakh cr, rates were expected to rise and corporate loans (29% of AUM) grow only ~16%.
_yieldOnAumWhy: Interest income ÷ average AUM was 12.1% in FY25, 11.3% in FY26 and 11.3% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis incl. fees: 13.10% → 12.68% → 12.58%) as the mix tilted to secured MSME and corporate loans. Management expects yields to rise only once personal & consumer loans (EIR ~16.2%) go from 14% back to 18-19% of AUM, 'a few more quarters'. We add 5bp a year for mix and gold loans.
_feeIncomePctWhy: Fee and other operating income (incl. the AMC dividend) ÷ average AUM: 0.92% in FY26 (0.71% excluding the ₹311 cr dividend); Q1FY27 ex-dividend run-rate 0.88% after a 60% jump in processing fees and insurance attachment. Build: fees 0.80% / 0.74% / 0.73% (FY28E cut by ~6bp for IRDAI's proposed caps on loan-linked insurance commission) + AMC dividend growing 10% a year (₹342 / 376 / 414 cr = 0.19% / 0.17% / 0.15% of average AUM).
_costOfFundsWhy: Interest expense ÷ average borrowings: 7.29% in FY26 (company: interest cost 6.62% of the average lending book). AAA-rated; Q1FY27 cost of funds fell 5bp QoQ. Most economists expected a 25bp repo hike in Oct-2026 (30% of borrowings are floating), so we hold FY27E flat and add 5bp in FY28E.
_opexPctWhy: Operating expenses incl. depreciation ÷ average AUM: 1.90% in FY26 and Q1FY27 (company: 1.93% / 1.95% of the lending book). Gold loans add 200-300 branches in FY27 and ~1,000 over three years, so we add 5-7bp before scale benefits return in FY29E.
_creditCostWhy: Impairment ÷ average AUM: 1.25% (FY25), 1.10% (FY26), 0.98% annualised in Q1FY27 (company basis 1.03%) after 18-24 months of cohort clean-up; GS3 1.30%, GS2+3 2.43%, PCR 48%. We assume 1.00% in FY27E rising to 1.10% by FY29E as unsecured and personal loans grow again and rates rise.
_taxRateWhy: FY26 effective rate 25.4% (₹1,059 cr on ₹4,168 cr); new regime 25.17%.
_payoutWhy: ABCL has never paid a dividend (Screener payout 0% FY15-FY26) and is raising equity to grow.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-operating other income ₹112 cr in FY26 and ₹134 cr in FY25 (Annual Report FY26), mainly interest on tax refunds and miscellaneous receipts; Screener shows ₹99 cr after the ₹12 cr labour-code charge.
_capitalRaiseWhy: ₹4,000 cr preferential allotment at ₹356.02 in June 2026 (11,23,53,236 shares: Grasim ₹2,880 cr on 23-Jun-2026, Suryaja ₹200 cr, IFC ₹920 cr). Management: no further raise needed for three years. ESOP allotments (a few lakh shares a quarter) ignored.

valuation._why: Cost of equity 13.4% (beta 1.15 as for other diversified NBFCs). The engine's justified P/B and residual income run on the STANDALONE book, which carries the subsidiaries at cost and earns only the AMC dividend on them, so they are a floor, not a fair value: sustainable standalone ROE 14% (NBFC ~16% on three-quarters of the book, ~3.5% dividend yield on the rest). The target is the sum of the parts; the engine has no SOTP method for lenders, so the SOTP value per share is carried as an implied multiple of standalone Sep-28E book (written by tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.sotp.js from the sotp block).

methods.name: SOTP as implied P/B
methods.why: SOTP value per share expressed as a multiple of standalone Sep-28E book (the engine has no SOTP for lenders): NBFC on P/B, ABHFL on P/B, AMC stake at market, ABSLI on P/EV, ABHI on P/GWP, less the holding discount. Multiples are set by tools/authoring/ABCAPITAL.sotp.js; see the valuation chapter.

methods.name: Justified P/B (standalone, subs at cost)
methods.why: (14 − 10) ÷ (13.4 − 10) on standalone Sep-27E book: values the subsidiaries at cost, so it is a floor.

methods.name: Residual income (standalone)
methods.why: Standalone book plus profits above a 13.4% cost of equity; subsidiaries at cost. A floor.

sotp._why: Sum of the parts on the house conventions: lending businesses on P/B of Sep-28E book (the house 12-month-forward basis); insurers on embedded value / premium at the 12-month target date (Sep-27E), because their multiples are trailing; listed stakes at the 30-Sep-2026 close; less a holding discount derived from ABCL's own history (ctx). Multiples derived in ABCAPITAL.ctx.js; a warning prints if these differ from the derivation.

nbfc._investWhy: Mar-26 ₹8,991 cr (Annual Report FY26 note 8); +₹608 cr of rights issues in Jul-2026 (ABSLI ₹484.5 cr, ABHI ₹123.9 cr) and ~₹500 cr a year after for the insurers and the digital platform (GAM estimate; 12.5% of the June raise is earmarked for subsidiaries).

hfc._why: AUM +50% YoY in Q1FY27 to ₹51,833 cr; target ₹1 lakh cr+ in 6-10 quarters at ~15% ROE; we model +39% / +30% / +26%. ROA 1.88% (FY26), 2.12% (Q1FY27); we use 2.0%. Book Mar-26 ₹5,979 cr + Advent's ₹2,750 cr (17-Apr-2026).

amc._why: Listed: ABCL's 12.96 cr ABSLAMC shares at the 30-Sep-2026 close. PAT path for the consolidated build only: +10% a year (FY26 ₹975 cr; Q1FY27 +12% YoY).

life._why: EV ₹15,447 cr at Mar-26 (operating RoEV 13.2%); we compound at 14% (VNB margin 15.1% in Q1 vs 7.5%, management targets >20% and doubling VNB in three years) plus the Jul-2026 rights issue (₹950 cr for 100%, ABCL's ₹484.5 cr). Economic variance (−₹934 cr in FY26) assumed zero.

health._why: Sales GWP ₹7,292 cr in FY26 (+39%), +50% in Q1FY27; we model +38% / +28% / +24%. Combined ratio 105% (FY26), 106% (Q1); management aims at 100% in FY27; IFRS profit ₹61 cr (FY26) → GAM path ₹150 / 300 / 450 cr.

money._why: Listed Aditya Birla Money (BIRLAMONEY) at the 30-Sep close; 5.65 cr shares (₹5.65 cr capital at ₹1 face value, AOC-1).

others._why: ARC at book (₹489 cr, AOC-1); the ABCD digital platform (FY26 loss ₹264 cr) at zero. 'Others' PAT for the consolidated build is the FY26 residual (−₹312 cr: ABCD, broking, ARC, eliminations) held roughly flat.

holdco._why: Derived in ABCAPITAL.ctx.js from ABCL's discount to look-through value at each quarter-end since Mar-2022 (constant multiples); a warning prints if these differ.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: NBFC AUM grows ~26% a year, margins widen as personal loans and gold rise, credit cost stays below 1%, IRDAI softens its caps; ABHFL reaches ₹1 lakh cr with 15% ROE; ABSLI margins move above 20%; the holding discount stays near today's level.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A rate-hike cycle and a turn in unsecured and MSME credit: AUM growth slows to ~17%, credit cost rises to ~1.5-1.6%, funding costs up 25bp and IRDAI's caps take most loan-linked insurance fees; insurers and HFC de-rate; the holding discount returns to its long-run median.
